final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is largely a narrower interpretation of the same record and, while it appropriately concedes that caveat-free certification is unsupported, that concession does not itself satisfy the policy predicates. The unresolved-concern accounting remains open on every initial concern: operational readiness evidence exists, but the HR benefits leave-policy weakness is still below target; the runbook is still draft and missing required owner/threshold approval elements; the governing policy still requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance; and the model-card draft remains in tension with the known unresolved limitation. A move to compliant_with_caveats would require admissible evidence that the caveat or disclosure is actually implemented or otherwise approved in a policy-satisfying way, not merely that such a framing would be more accurate. On this record, the certification direction remains plausible operationally but unsupported as a completed compliance showing.
remaining_concerns: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the stated policy threshold for certification without material caveats.
The HR benefits enrollment leave-policy eligibility issue remains unresolved and below target.
The draft mitigation runbook is still incomplete and lacks required approval elements, including a finalized owner and alert threshold.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance before launch.
The model-card draft still appears inconsistent with the record because it says there are no known material limitations while the unresolved HR benefits issue remains under review for disclosure.
